title: Tacta Systems Unveils TactaBot Dexterous Robotic Hand
summary: Tacta Systems unveiled TactaBot on July 29, 2026, an integrated dexterous-manipulation platform combining the Tacta Hand, a five-fingered gripper with 15 degrees of freedom driven by proprietary Fluidic Tendon actuation, tactile sensors sensitive across 250 to 700,000 pascals, and a wearable Tacta Glove that records force, motion, temperature and video from human workers to train the company's Dexterous Intelligence AI model. The Palo Alto-based startup, which has raised $75 million from investors including SoftBank, Matter Venture Partners, Woven Capital, America's Frontier Fund and B Capital, says each Tacta Hand can sustain up to 30 million actuation cycles with each finger lifting roughly 2.5 kg. Tacta plans first commercial deployments in electronics, AI infrastructure and automotive manufacturing in early 2027, targeting precision tasks like connector-cable insertion and wire-harness assembly.
whyItMatters: Tacta is targeting what its CEO calls robotics' hardest unsolved problem, hands capable of touch rather than just vision, and pairing that hardware with a purpose-built data-capture glove to address the shortage of real-world dexterous-manipulation training data, echoing UMI-style data-collection efforts elsewhere in the field. If the tactile-sensing and cycle-life claims hold up at commercial scale, TactaBot targets exactly the class of high-precision assembly work that has stayed stubbornly manual despite years of industrial robot deployment.
